question.prompt: If \(x,\) \(y\) and \(2x+\frac y2\) are not zero, then \[ \left(2x+\frac y2\right)^{-1}\left[(2x)^{-1}+\left(\frac y2\right)^{-1}\right] \] equals

solutions.explanation:
The exponent \(-1\) means reciprocal. Put \(u=2x\) and \(v=y/2\). The given conditions ensure that \(u\), \(v\), and \(u+v\) are nonzero, and \(uv=xy\).

Adding the reciprocals produces \(u+v\) in the numerator, which cancels the outside denominator:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\frac1{u+v}\left(\frac1u+\frac1v\right)
&=\frac1{u+v}\cdot\frac{u+v}{uv}\\
&=\frac1{uv}\\
&=\frac1{xy}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The cancellation is valid because \(u+v\ne0\). Thus the expression equals \((xy)^{-1}\), choice D.
solutions.title: Combine the reciprocals
